inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Infant Daily Report - Infant's Mood: Several of the infants' daily reports did not include the mood for the infants, and one infant's daily report did not have a summary of daily activities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Daily Report - Infant's Mood (26 TAC §746.2431(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Postings-Child's Food Allergies: One child had an allergy, and the information was stored in a folder in their classroom instead of posted in their classroom. This was corrected during the inspection when the child's allergy plan was posted in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Postings-Child's Food Allergies (26 TAC §746.401(10))

occurrences.finding: First Aid Kit - Supplies Not Expired: The antiseptic wipes in the first aid kit had expired in 2025. This was corrected during the inspection when the wipes were disposed of and new wipes were placed in the first aid kit.
occurrences.violation_type_title: First Aid Kit - Supplies Not Expired (26 TAC §746.4003(b))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: During a DFPS investigation, video shows a caregiver grabbing and pulling a child aggressively.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: During a DFPS investigation, it was found that a caregiver was on their phone while caring for children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: A caregiver stated they were unaware of how many children they were responsible for. This was corrected during the inspection when I counted the children and informed the caregiver that they had ten children in their class.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: One infant's feeding instructions were last updated in July.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation, there was sufficient evidence found to determine that two children left their class, got outside the daycare, and were outside unsupervised for approximately six minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to determine that a caregiver disciplined two children by not letting them finish eating their meal after one of the children spilled a cup of milk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to determine that a caregiver roughly grabbed a child out of her chair and pulled her away from the table.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children: During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to determine that a caregiver did not relate to children with respect and patience when the caregiver snatched a child's cup of milk away and spoke to the children in an impatient, disrespectful tone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children (26 TAC §746.1201(2))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to determine that a caregiver was using a cell phone while supervising children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to determine that a caregiver did not demonstrate good judgment when she reached into a bowl of food intended for children, ate some, and then served the children from the same bowl.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Medication No Longer Used: There was expired medication and medication that children were no longer using stored in the office. This was corrected during the inspection when the medication was disposed of.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication No Longer Used (26 TAC §746.3809)

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The operation's last annual fire inspection was done on 10/3/23.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation, there was sufficient evidence found to determine that a child was able to get into a storage room that was secured from the inside with a block of wood before the child's caregiver intervened.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: During the investigation, there was sufficient evidence found to determine that a caregiver used inappropriate discipline when she dragged a child to her, lifted him by one arm, and carried him across the room by one arm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Animals: The operation did not have a policy informing parents that an animal is present on the premesis.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Animals (26 TAC §746.501(a)(17))

occurrences.finding: Maximum Height - Under Age 2: The playscape, in the playground area, is designed for children 3 years old and older. During the inspection children 18 months to 2 years old were observed on the playscape. The Director placed another caregiver on the playground to assist with providing the children with alternate activities and the children were removed from the playscape.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maximum Height - Under Age 2 (26 TAC §746.4607(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: It was determined the caregiver did not have the appropriate proximity to the children in order to intervene, during the times the children were biting. The ratio in the classroom was 4 to 1. At times, the classroom had 2 caregivers and biting was still occurring frequently.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: Based on evidence obtained, it was determined a caregiver will tap children harshly on their shoulder with an open hand, when they do not follow directions given.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Praise and Encouragement: Based on the evidence obtained it was determined a Caregiver will yell at the children in the classroom when they do not listen to instruction and loses her patience.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Use Praise and Encouragement (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(A))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: During an investigation, it was determined a child was hit on the thigh by the open hand of a caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: During an investigation, sufficient evidence was found that a child was abused.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities: Observed children in care transition from outdoor play to nap time without washing hands prior to going to cots. This was corrected by the caregiver taking children to the restroom to wash hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities (26 TAC §746.3417(4))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on the information gathered during the investigation it was determined that the operation did not notify parents allegations that placed a child at risk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on the information gathered during the investigation it was determined that the operation did not notify licensing of allegations that placed a child at risk
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups: During the inspection the infant bottles were not labeled. This was corrected by the caregiver labeling the bottles.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups (26 TAC §746.2419(6))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal: During the inspection the last fire marshal inspection was completed in July 2021.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal (26 TAC §746.5101(b))

occurrences.finding: Requirement of Gas Leak Inspection: During the inspection it was found that the last gas inpsection was completed in March 2020.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirement of Gas Leak Inspection (26 TAC §746.5401)

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Children's Records: During the inspection the children records were missing the following required documents: Immunizations and  health statements
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Children's Records (26 TAC §746.801(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records: During the inspection it was found that the personnel files were not being maintained and the following required documents were missing: date of hire, proof of pre-service exemption, orientation, high school diplomas, proof of trainings within the first 90 days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: Based on the information gathered during the investigation it was found that the operation did not notify licensing within the required timeframe of a child injured at the operation and going to the emergency room for medical care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Children's Products- Annual Certification: The operation did not have documentation that the consumer product safety had been reviewed with the required time frame.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Annual Certification (26 TAC §746.4135(b))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Never Unsupervised: Observed infants sleeping in a room next to the infant playroom with a wall that blocks the view of infants sleeping and the caregiver was observed on the playroom side  leaving the infants unspervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Never Unsupervised (26 TAC §746.2401(7))
